$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Quantity in an Expression Involving the Dot Product
questions.problem:
Let $v=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 2x \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}3x \\ -3 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
If $v\cdot w=-2$ and $x>0$, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $v\cdot w=-2,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot w & =-2 \\ x\cdot 3x+2x\cdot (-3)+4\cdot x+(-5)\cdot 2 & =-2 \\ 3{x}^{2}-6x+4x-10 & =-2 \\ 3{x}^{2}-2x-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-(-2)\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(3)(-8)}}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{100}}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 10}{6} \\  & =\frac{1\pm 5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get two solutions, ${x}_{1}=-\frac{4}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=2.$ Since we need $x>0$, our final answer is $x=2$ only.

questions.problem:
Let $u=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 3t \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}t \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ {t}^{2} \\ 5\end{aligned}].$
If $u\cdot v=-2$ and $t>3$, find the value of $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $u\cdot v=-2,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $t$ and then solve for $t$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =-2 \\ 7\cdot t+9\cdot 2+3t\cdot (-5)+1\cdot {t}^{2}+(-1)\cdot 5 & =-2 \\ 7t+18-15t+{t}^{2}-5 & =-2 \\ {t}^{2}-8t+15 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We get two solutions, ${t}_{1}=3$ and ${t}_{2}=5.$ Since we need $t>3$, our final answer is $t=5$ only.

questions.problem:
Let $l=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ x \\ 2 \\ x \\ 2x\end{aligned}]$ and $m=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ x \\ 4 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$
If $l\cdot m=3$ and $x>3$, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $l\cdot m=3,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}l\cdot m & =3 \\ 5\cdot 1+x\cdot x+2\cdot 4+x\cdot (-1)+2x\cdot (-3) & =3 \\ 5+{x}^{2}+8-x-6x & =3 \\ {x}^{2}-7x+13 & =3 \\ {x}^{2}-7x+10 & =0 \\ (x-5)(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We get two solutions, ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2.$ Since we need $x>3$, our final answer is $x=5$ only.

$$

$$

We get two solutions, ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=6.$ Since we need $x<6$, our final answer is $x=2$ only.

questions.problem:
Let
$p=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ y-3 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -4 \\ y\end{aligned}].$
If $p\cdot q=0$, find the value of $y.$
questions.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $p\cdot q=0,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $y$ and then solve for $y$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 9\cdot 0+(y-3)\cdot 1+3\cdot (-4)+4\cdot y & =0 \\ y-3-12+4y & =0 \\ 5y & =15 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y=3.$

Multiplying each component of $\mathbf{a}$ by $\dfrac{1}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}a & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-4) \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 6 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 3 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

First, we multiply each component of $\mathbf{a}$ by $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and each component of $\mathbf{b}$ by $\dfrac{1}{2}.$ Then, we add the vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}a+\frac{1}{2}b & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ 12 \\ -9 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -6 \\ 2 \\ -8 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-2 \\ 2-3 \\ 4+1 \\ -3-4 \\ 1+5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 5 \\ -7 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let be $[\begin{aligned}10 \\ x \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}x \\ x \\ 8 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ If $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=0,$ find the value of $x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=0,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 10\cdot x+x\cdot x+0\cdot 8+5\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 10x+{x}^{2}+25 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+10x+25 & =0 \\ (x+5)^{2} & =0 \\ x & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $x=-5.$
